title: Noise-aware paging orchestration and adaptive circuit-breaker hysteresis
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: Reduce noisy pages and improve automated mitigation by combining SLO-aware alert thresholds, an adaptive hysteresis layer for circuit-breakers, and an automated on-call orchestration runbook. This ticket implements the orchestration glue and codifies the runbook automation so that alerts transition from noisy signal bursts to meaningful on-call actions with automated containment and progressive escalation.
acceptance_criteria: A. Paging noise reduced by >= 60% for the top-10 noisy alerts in staging while SLO error budget burn detection remains >= 95% recall
B. Circuit-breakers expose a tunable hysteresis window that adapts to rolling 10m tail-latency and QPS; changes verified via canary in prod-dry run

C. Automated runbook executes containment actions (route-level shedding, model fallback, cross-region reroute) without manual approval in low-impact failures and creates a Linear incident with pre-populated diagnostics in high-impact failures
D. Dashboards (per-route SLO heatmap + paging noise) and a post-deployment Playbook doc exist and are linked in the ticket
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument: ensure per-route metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, qps, queue-length) are surfaced to metrics pipeline with 15s granularity

2) Classifier: deploy a simple rules+ML hybrid 'noise filter' that tags alerts as likely-noise vs true-regression using historical alert context (frequency, duplication, time-of-day, deploys). Build in a manual override in Console

3) Adaptive hysteresis: add a hysteresis controller that widens the circuit-breaker cool-down when repeated transient spikes are observed; narrow when stable. Hysteresis parameters exposed via feature-flag and runtime-config for per-region and per-customer tiers

4) Runbook automation: implement runbook runner hooks that perform containment (route-level load-shedding, model fallback to quantized variant, cross-region routing) and create a Linear incident with diagnostic snapshot. Provide safe-guards to avoid automated action during ongoing deploy windows
5) Canary & Dry Run: run canary in prod-dry (10% traffic) for 48h and run a series of synthetic failure scenarios (KV cache pressure, cold-start storm, one-region latency spike) to validate behavior
6) Rollout: staged rollout by route groups (low-risk -> medium -> high-risk) with telemetry gating and automatic rollback if error budget burn jumps > 5% in 30m
design_decisions: Decision: Use hybrid ML+rules filter rather than pure ML to keep deterministic overrides and faster iteration during oncall
Decision: Hysteresis controller adjusts cool-down multiplicatively (x1.5 on repeat transient, x0.7 on stable window) to avoid oscillation
Decision: Automated containment allowed for 'low' and 'medium' customer-impact routes; 'high' impact requires manual confirm from on-call
Trade-off: Longer hysteresis windows reduce pages but can delay recovery for genuine incidents. We mitigate by tying hysteresis to several signals (error budget consumption, p99 drift, deploy flag)
test_plan: Unit tests for hysteresis math, edge cases where QPS drops to zero
Integration tests: simulate region failover and validate circuit-breaker opens and recovers per policy
Chaos scenarios: introduce injected 30% latency on region-west and confirm automatic cross-region reroute triggers without pager for low-impact routes
Canary: 48h in prod-dry with synthetic workload and daily review notes
rollout_steps: Staged rollout to route groups with 1-hour telemetry gating
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: 'Paging Noise & SLO Heatmap' (per-route) - link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/paging-noise/slo-heatmap
Alerting: Add meta-alerts that fire when automated containment triggers > 3 times in 1h
SLO reporting: add dimension for 'alert-filtered' vs 'raw' to show effect of noise filter on signal fidelity
runbook_summary: Automated Runbook: (1) On noisy alert detection, run 'noise classifier' - if classified as noise, de-dupe and suppress repeat pages for 20m with exponential backoff. (2) If classified as real and error budget burn > 1%/10m, trigger containment: route-level shedding -> model fallback -> cross-region reroute. (3) Create Incident in Linear with diagnostics and notify primary on-call. Follow escalation ladder unless the automated containment resolves the issue.
oncall_steps: Step 0: Confirm automation actions from console activity log
Step 1: If automation performed containment, review 'containment rationale' snapshot and check SLO heatmap
Step 2: If automation did not resolve and impact is high, promote incident to Major and follow Major Incident playbook
Step 3: If false positive paging suspected, mark rule as 'suppress for cadence' for 24h and open follow-up ticket with classifier false-positive evidence
postmortem_requirements: If incident led to > 5% additional SLO burn for any customer tier or >1 hour of degraded throughput, produce postmortem within 72h
Include classifier confusion matrix, hysteresis parameter history, and containment timeline
